title: Induction of Innate Immune Memory in Human Smooth Muscle and Endothelial Cells In Vitro
author: Sonnenberg, Schwarz, et al.
materials: Human vascular smooth muscle cell basal medium
EBM-2 endothelial cell growth basal medium-2

steps.title: Prepare laboratory and reagents
steps.instruction: Gather all required reagents, start the cell‑culture laminar‑flow hood, disinfect the work surface and pipettes, ensure all consumables are sterile, prepare media and solutions, set a water bath to 37 °C and pre‑warm the culture medium.

steps.title: Thaw and seed cryopreserved vascular cells
steps.instruction: Add 13 mL of SMGM (for smooth‑muscle cells) or ECGM (for HAECs/HUVECs) to a 75 cm² flask (or a precoated flask for endothelial cells) and equilibrate in a 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator for ≥30 min. Retrieve a cryovial from liquid nitrogen (‑196 °C), twist the cap partially open to relieve pressure, then place the vial in a 37 °C water bath for 2 min. Wipe the vial with 70 % ethanol and open it inside the sterile hood. Resuspend the cells gently with a 1000 µL pipette, dispense the suspension into the pre‑warmed flask, loosely tighten the cap, and move the flask in a cross‑like pattern to distribute cells homogeneously. Return the flask to the incubator. The next day replace the medium to remove DMSO residue and unattached cells. (Optional) Transfer the thawed content to a 15 mL tube, add PBS or medium, centrifuge at 350 g for 5 min, discard the DMSO‑containing supernatant, resuspend the pellet in fresh SMGM/ECGM and seed the flask (this skips the direct‑dispense step but may cause cell loss). Replace the medium every 2–3 days until cells reach 80–90 % confluency for sub‑cultivation. Note that high DMSO concentrations can impair growth and viability.

substeps.instruction: Add 13 mL SMGM or ECGM to flask and equilibrate ≥30 min at 37 °C, 5 % CO₂.
Thaw cryovial in 37 °C water bath for 2 min (after partial cap opening).
Disinfect vial with 70 % ethanol, open in sterile hood.
Dispense cells into flask, loosely tighten cap.
Rock flask in cross‑like pattern to spread cells.
Next day refresh medium to remove DMSO and unattached cells.
Optional: Transfer to 15 mL tube, add PBS/medium, centrifuge 350 g 5 min, discard DMSO supernatant, resuspend and seed.
Replace medium every 2–3 days until 80–90 % confluency.

steps.title: Culture cells to desired confluency
steps.instruction: Maintain the seeded cells in a humidified 37 °C, 5 % CO₂ incubator, changing the medium every 2–3 days until they reach 80–90 % confluency, at which point they are ready for priming or restimulation.

steps.title: Prepare restimulation medium with TLR agonist
steps.instruction: Add either 5 µg/mL Pam3Cys4 (TLR2 agonist) or 10 ng/mL LPS (TLR4 agonist) to the appropriate resting medium for the cell type to create the restimulation medium.

steps.title: Restimulate cells and avoid disturbance
steps.instruction: Replace the existing culture medium with the Pam3Cys4‑containing medium (or LPS medium). Do not touch the cell layer with pipettes, do not let the cells dry out, and if using a suction pump avoid completely drying the well.

steps.title: Harvest cells for RNA or ELISA
steps.instruction: Four to six hours after restimulation lyse the cells with an appropriate lysis buffer for RNA isolation and/or qPCR; process lysates immediately or store at ‑80 °C. Twenty‑four hours after restimulation collect supernatants for ELISA; assay immediately or freeze at ‑20 °C.

substeps.instruction: At 4–6 h post‑restimulation, lyse cells with RNA‑compatible buffer.
Process lysate immediately or store at ‑80 °C.
At 24 h post‑restimulation, collect supernatant for ELISA.
Assay ELISA immediately or freeze supernatant at ‑20 °C.

steps.title: Normalize ELISA data with Calcein AM
steps.instruction: Stain adherent cells with 1 µM Calcein AM prepared in warm 1 % BSA in PBS (pH 7.4), incubate plates at 37 °C for 20 min, then measure fluorescence using FITC/Alexa Fluor 488 filters; use the fluorescence intensity to normalize cytokine levels to the number of viable cells.

substeps.instruction: Add appropriate volume of 1 µM Calcein AM in 1 % BSA/PBS (pH 7.4).
Measure fluorescence with FITC/Alexa Fluor 488 filter set.

steps.title: Analyze ELISA data with logistic regression
steps.instruction: Process raw ELISA values using software capable of four‑parameter logistic regression (e.g., WorkOut 2.5 or MyAssays online) to generate cytokine concentrations; account for donor variability and report mean ± SD.

description: Innate immune memory/trained immunity is a newly described phenomenon that has evolved very fast during the last decade.3 Growing evidence shows that innate immune cells as well as vascular cells can develop a memory-like phenotype in response to different inflammatory stimuli.1,2 The memory is induced through epigenetic modifications in the histones and cellular metabolic changes, which enables the trained cells to exhibit enhanced inflammatory reactions in response to a secondary stimulus.4,5 Although development of innate immune memory is beneficial in improving host responses to an infection, it can contribute in inflammatory diseases onset and development. Therefore, current knowledge suggests trained immunity as an approach to prevent and treat the diseases. The protocol below states the step-by-step instructions for inducing trained immunity in vascular cells. All procedures are performed in a Class I biological safety hood with standard aseptic technique and cells are cultured in a humidified 37°C incubator with 5% CO2.
